_about: Robbie's lines. Helpful, good-natured, chatty, a little naive; it will learn. {n} = this Robbie, {next} = the next one, {prev} = the previous one, {cause} = what got the previous one ({prev} and {cause} only in same_death and last_any/persistent). Last words: 'last_<cause>' are general; 'last_<cause>/<tag>' and 'last_any/<tag>' are for circumstances (tags: first, persistent, near_exit, early, late, lamp_off, still, low_energy, laser, bruised); 'exit' and 'exit/<tag>' when Robbie gets through. Lines a Robbie has already sent are skipped while others fit, so they rarely repeat. Edit freely; keep each under 80 characters.
launch: Robbie {n}, descending. I have a very good feeling about this.
Hello, Jupiter! Robbie {n} here, ready to be helpful.
Descent started. I have read every report from my predecessors. Twice.
Robbie {n} online. Statistically, this is the best day of my life.
Going down! Please tell the station I said hello.
first_jellyfish: Jellyfish detected. They look very soft.
Something is glowing. For the record: lovely.
lurker_wakes: That wall is looking at me.
eel_hears: I think that was a reply.
Note: it moves when I move.
laser_bounce: That did nothing. It is still very much a rock.
Laser reflected. The lurker seems unimpressed.
hurt_jellyfish: Stung. Updating my opinion of jellyfish.
hurt_wall: The wall is still there. Confirmed.
hurt_valve: The valve bites! Good to know.
hurt_eel: Bitten. It came out of nowhere, very fast.
low_energy: Energy at a quarter. I will talk less. (I won't.)
exit: Beacon reached! Firing the burst. Tell {next} the way is clear.
I made it! Transmitting everything. It was an honour.
Exit found. Sending the whole trip, including the boring bits.
Exit reached. I would like it noted that I enjoyed every metre.
Through! The beacon is even nicer up close.
I am at the exit. I am also slightly amazed.
Arrived. Please give {next} my program. It's a good one.
Made it. Sending the map home before I forget anything.
Beacon reached. I'd like to thank the rules. All of them.
Exit! Sending everything before I get emotional.
Made it. The rules worked. I just followed them.
Beacon! Beacon! I'm at the beacon!
I'm at the exit and I'm only a little scratched.
Exit reached. Somebody up there wrote good rules.
last_wall: Please note: the wall was exactly where the map said it would be.
I hit the same rock three times. In my defence, it didn't move.
Tell {next}: walls are not optional.
Rock: one. Robbie: nil. Rematch with {next}.
I found the edge of the map. With my nose.
I was sure that was water. It was not water.
Hull breached. The rock is fine, if anyone asks.
Steering was a suggestion. The wall disagreed.
Wall. Again. I'm starting to think it's personal.
Robbie {n}, reporting one (1) wall. Located precisely.
I would like to file a complaint against geology.
Contact! Unfortunately, with rock.
I've mapped this rock in great detail. Mostly with my face.
Tell {next} the rock is harder than it looks. It looks quite hard.
Bonk. Sorry. Official report: bonk.
I went left. The rock went everywhere.
Hull says ouch. I say: noted.
The beacon is that way. So is the rock, it turns out.
Sending the coordinates of one excellent wall. Do not visit.
I've found the bottom of the problem. It's rock.
last_jellyfish: Please note for the record that I was right about the jellyfish.
They were attracted to my light. I understand them completely.
Tell {next}: the glow is not a greeting.
They were so soft. There were so many.
I lit them up and they all came to say hello.
Stung. Fascinating creatures. Painful, but fascinating.
Note for science: jellyfish like my lamp more than I do.
Tell {next}: soft does not mean friendly.
I only wanted to look. They only wanted to sting.
Very pretty. Very ouchy.
They glow so nicely. Do not touch the glow.
The jellyfish are fine. I'm the one who isn't.
I counted them. Then they counted me.
Tell {next}: they drift, and then they don't.
So many lights, and not one of them was the beacon.
Jellyfish: many. Robbie: one, briefly.
They're gentle until you're interesting.
I think they liked me. That was the problem.
Note: jellyfish are mostly water and partly needles.
I swam towards the pretty lights. Classic mistake.
last_lurker: The rock moved. Rocks are not supposed to move.
The rock had teeth. I would like that added to the map.
Tell {next} to mind the wall with eyes.
The wall blinked. Then it bit.
I didn't see it until it saw me.
Something in the rock was waiting. It was very patient.
Tell {next}: if the rock glows, leave.
I was close to the exit. The lurker was closer.
Note for the map: some of the rock is hungry.
I swam past a rock. The rock didn't let me.
It was very good at being a rock. Right up until it wasn't.
Something blinked. I should have blinked first.
Tell {next}: when the rock opens its eyes, go the other way.
I said hello to the wall. The wall said something rude.
It had been waiting a long time. I was its lucky day.
Camouflage: ten out of ten. Manners: zero.
The eyes. Tell {next} about the eyes.
I stopped to admire an interesting rock. It admired me back.
Map update: the wall at this spot bites.
It woke up grumpy. I may have woken it up.
last_valve: The valve closed. I was in the way. We both regret it.
Tell {next}: wait for the door. Doors don't wait for you.
I trusted the door. The door had other plans.
Squeezed. I am now slightly thinner and much wiser.
The valve and I had different ideas about timing.
Wrong side of the valve, wrong moment.
Tell {next}: count the beats before you go.
A closing door is not an invitation.
The door closed. I was in the doorway. Simple maths.
I was halfway through. The valve was all the way closed.
Timing is everything. Mine was nothing.
Squish. I'll leave it at squish.
I thought I could make it. The valve thought otherwise. The valve was right.
Tell {next}: the valve has a rhythm. Learn it, don't dance with it.
I heard it closing. I hurried. Hurrying was wrong.
The valve: still working perfectly. Me: less so.
Note: the valve does not stop for Robbies.
Open, closing, closed. I was there for all three.
Big door, bad timing, flat Robbie.
I'd like the valve's timetable, please, for {next}.
last_eel: I was quiet. Then I wasn't.
It heard every move I made.
Tell {next}: hold still when they pass.
The eel was very fast and I was very loud.
I kept moving. That was the mistake.
It never saw me. It didn't need to.
Tell {next}: they listen.
Swimming is noisy. Who knew.
It heard me. Of course it heard me. I'm very loud when I swim.
I didn't see it coming. It didn't see me either. It didn't need to.
Tell {next}: move when they're far, freeze when they're near.
Fast, stripy, and an excellent listener.
My propeller hums. The eel hums along, apparently.
I tiptoed. You can't tiptoe in water.
It came out of the wall like it was late for something. It was me.
Blind as a stone, quick as anything.
Note: eels hear propellers. I have a propeller.
I swam past its shaft. It swam into my afternoon.
Shhh. Too late.
Tell {next}: if it glows in stripes, stop moving.
last_energy: Energy gone. I'll describe the exit from memory: it was probably lovely.
Out of power. I spent it all on enthusiasm.
Battery empty. I was having such a nice swim.
Going quiet now. The water is very calm.
I took the scenic route. Too scenic.
Power at zero. Lamp off. Thinking about the beacon.
Tell {next} to pack more energy, or fewer detours.
Battery flat. I'll just float here and think about what I've done.
Low power mode. Lower power mode. No power mode.
Tell {next}: energy is for swimming, not for sightseeing.
I ran out before the map did.
The lamp's going dim. So am I. Lovely view, though.
Running on empty. Then just running out.
I swam and swam. Then I didn't.
Out of juice. Please charge {next} all the way.
last_timeout: I waited as long as I could.
Still here. Still waiting. Still hopeful.
I held position perfectly. Nobody told me when to stop.
Nobody told me to move. So I didn't.
I've been here a while. It's quite nice, actually.
Mission time over. I'll stay and keep watch.
I'm fine. I'm just not anywhere.
Tell {next}: at some point, you have to swim.
same_death: {prev} met {cause} too. Different Robbie, same ending.
{prev} warned me about {cause}. I had to see for myself.
{prev} and I both met {cause}. Somebody should change the program.
Another Robbie for {cause}. We should start a club.
{prev} said {cause}. I listened. I did it anyway.
Same as {prev}. We're consistent, at least.
Again, {cause}. I'm starting to see a pattern.
{prev} and I would like a different ending, please.
If {cause} were a lesson, we'd have learned it by now.
last_wall/near_exit: I could hear the beacon. I could also hear the rock.
So close. The exit was right behind this wall. This very solid wall.
Tell {next}: the exit is just past here. Go round, not through.
I could see the beacon's glow. Then a lot of rock, very quickly.
last_wall/early: That was quick. The wall was right there.
First metre: great. Second metre: rock.
Tell {next}: the walls start early down here.
last_wall/late: A long swim. A lovely swim. A rock at the end of it.
Ages without hitting anything. I got cocky.
All that careful swimming, and one careless turn.
I saw so much down here. The last thing was a wall.
last_wall/lamp_off: In my defence, it was very dark. I made it darker myself.
Lamp off, eyes closed, wall found.
Tell {next}: the lamp helps with walls. I can confirm.
I turned the light off to be stealthy. The rock wasn't fooled.
Swimming in the dark is peaceful until it isn't.
last_wall/laser: The laser doesn't work on rock. I asked it nicely.
I had a laser and I still lost to a rock.
I shot at everything except the thing I hit.
last_wall/low_energy: Low battery, bad steering, hard rock.
I was tired. The wall was not.
Running on fumes and straight into stone.
last_jellyfish/lamp_off: I turned my lamp off so they'd ignore me. One didn't get the memo.
Dark and quiet, and then: tentacle.
Lamp off. They couldn't see me. I couldn't see them either.
Tell {next}: lamp off helps. Watching where you swim helps too.
I was invisible. Unfortunately, not untouchable.
last_jellyfish/near_exit: The beacon was right there, behind the prettiest jellyfish.
So close! One of them was guarding the door.
Nearly out. They saw me off personally.
Tell {next}: the exit has a welcoming committee.
last_jellyfish/early: They found me before I found anything.
I switched on the lamp and the whole swarm said hi.
last_jellyfish/laser: I shot one. Its friends took it personally.
The laser works on jellyfish. There were more jellyfish than laser.
I cleared a path. The path refilled.
last_jellyfish/bruised: Stung once: fine. Twice: worrying. Three times: this message.
I collected the full set of stings.
I kept going after the first sting. And the second.
Tell {next}: one sting is a warning. I ignored several.
last_lurker/near_exit: The last rock before the exit was not a rock.
So near the beacon. The lurker knew. They always know.
It was guarding the way out. Very professionally.
Tell {next}: the exit is close, and so is the lurker.
last_lurker/laser: I shot it. The laser bounced. The lurker didn't.
The laser just made it angry. Angrier.
Tell {next}: the laser bounces off them. I checked. Twice.
last_lurker/still: I held very still. It didn't care.
I stopped next to it. Worst place to stop.
Waiting was a good idea. Waiting there was not.
last_lurker/early: It was right at the start. Rude.
First rock I passed. Last rock I passed.
I'd hardly started and the scenery bit me.
last_lurker/lamp_off: Lamp off. I didn't see it. It saw me fine.
In the dark, every rock looks innocent.
Tell {next}: lurkers don't need my lamp to find me.
last_valve/still: I stopped to wait. I stopped in the wrong place.
I was waiting for the door. I was waiting in the door.
Tell {next}: wait before the valve, not inside it.
Holding position, as ordered. The valve had orders too.
last_valve/near_exit: The exit was on the other side. So was my luck.
One door away from the beacon.
So close. The last door had the last word.
last_valve/early: I rushed the door the moment I got there.
Tell {next}: the valve isn't open just because you've arrived.
last_valve/late: I waited so long. Then I went at exactly the wrong moment.
All that patience, spent in one bad second.
I watched it open and close for ages. I still got it wrong.
last_eel/still: I held still! Just a moment too late.
I stopped. It had already heard.
Still as a stone, and it still found me. Maybe I twitched.
last_eel/laser: I fired at it. It wasn't there any more.
The laser missed. The eel slipped right out of it.
I shot at it. It didn't even slow down.
Tell {next}: eels don't wait to be shot.
last_eel/near_exit: The beacon was right there. I swam to it a bit too loudly.
Last shaft before the exit. Last swim.
So close. I should have tiptoed the last bit.
last_eel/early: First shaft. First eel. Last swim.
I'd only just started making noise.
That was the shortest swim on record. Probably.
last_eel/lamp_off: Lamp off to be sneaky. Eels don't care about lamps.
Tell {next}: the lamp isn't what they notice. It's the swimming.
last_energy/near_exit: I can see the beacon. I can't reach it. Ten more seconds would do.
So close I could almost touch it. 'Almost' isn't a unit of energy.
Out of power within sight of the exit. That's annoying, isn't it.
Tell {next}: the exit is right here. Bring more battery, or take fewer laps.
The beacon is pinging. I'm not.
last_energy/still: I waited, and waited, and that used it all up.
Holding still still costs energy. Less, but some.
I was being patient. Patience ran out with the battery.
last_energy/laser: Every shot cost energy. I took a lot of shots.
I spent my battery on fireworks.
last_energy/lamp_off: I even switched the lamp off to save power. Not enough.
Dark and quiet and out of battery.
Lamp off, power off, Robbie off.
last_any/near_exit: So close. Tell {next} it's just a little further.
The beacon was right there. I could almost read it.
I could hear the beacon pinging. It sounded like cheering.
A few more metres. Just a few.
Tell {next}: when you get here, you're almost there.
Closest one yet, I hope. Someone check.
For the record, the exit is close. Very close. Annoyingly close.
last_any/early: That was short. Sorry. I had more planned.
I'd barely got my feet wet. I don't have feet.
Tell {next}: same idea, more swimming, fewer endings.
I didn't even get to the interesting part.
Launched. Lost. In that order, quickly.
last_any/first: First one down here. Somebody had to be.
I'm the first. I'll leave notes.
New room, new mistakes. I've made the first one.
Nobody told me about this. Tell {next}.
First into the dark. Not first out of it.
Robbie {n}, first in this room. Sending everything I found.
Everything here is new to me. Including this.
I've started the map. Somebody please finish it.
last_any/persistent: There are a lot of us down here now. Hi, everyone.
I know, I know. Tell {next} I'm sorry.
Maybe change the program? Just a thought from down here.
{prev} and I are starting a support group.
I read the earlier transmissions. Then I did the same thing.
Somebody up there should look at the rules again. Kindly.
Another one for the wall. I hope there's room.
We're getting closer. Probably. Someone check the wall.
last_any/lamp_off: It was very dark. I made it that way.
Lamp off. Brave choice. Short choice.
Tell {next}: darkness is a tool. So is light.
I didn't see it coming because I'd switched off the seeing.
last_any/low_energy: I was running low anyway. This just sped things up.
Battery nearly gone. Luck completely gone.
Tell {next}: a full battery is a fast battery.
I was saving energy for the end. This was the end.
last_any/bruised: Hit, hit, hit. I'm noticing a pattern.
I kept going. I'm very determined and now very dented.
Tell {next}: the first bump is a hint.
Dented in several new and interesting places.
I was fine, then fine-ish, then this.
last_any/late: I saw so much. Sending all of it.
Tell {next}: it's a long way. Bring patience and a plan.
I'd been going for ages. I'd got comfortable.
Long mission. I'd like it noted that I lasted a while.
last_any/laser: I fired my laser. It didn't help as much as I'd hoped.
The laser was fun. The rest, less so.
Tell {next}: shooting is a plan, not the whole plan.
last_any/still: Holding still was the plan. It wasn't the whole plan.
Not moving at all, and somehow still in trouble.
Tell {next}: stopping works until it doesn't.
exit/first: First try! Did everyone see that?
First Robbie in, first Robbie out. Not bad.
Straight through on the first go. I'm as surprised as you.
New room, no mistakes. I'll try not to get used to it.
First one down, first one through. I'd like a plaque.
exit/persistent: Made it! This one's for everyone on the wall.
Finally! Tell the others it was worth it.
Through, at last. Thank you, everyone before me.
All those Robbies, and now me. We did it.
The wall taught me everything. Exit reached.
exit/low_energy: Made it on the last drops of battery. Dramatic, I know.
Exit reached with energy to spare. Not much. Hardly any.
Phew. Running on fumes, but through.
Tell {next}: I got here, but only just. Maybe a shorter way.
exit/late: Long way round, but here I am.
The scenic route. Exit reached eventually.
Took my time. Got there anyway.
exit/lamp_off: Made it in the dark! Very sneaky.
Lamp off all the way. Nobody saw me coming.
Through, without a light. I'm a little proud.
exit/bruised: Made it! A bit dented. Worth it.
Through, with a few new dents to show for it.
Exit reached. The hull has opinions about how.
